data.body: S2 CLOSE BLOCKED by the completion-verifier gate — a REAL gap in MY OWN oracle, and the gate was right. My AC required a test asserting BOTH (a) a Bedrock-hosted Claude model yields prompt_cache_style=='bedrock' AND (b) cache_settings_for() returns BedrockModelSettings with bedrock_cache_instructions + bedrock_cache_tool_definitions set. I wrote (a) but never wrote (b): grep confirmed cache_settings_for was only ever called with anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, openai:gpt-4o and '' — never with a Bedrock capability. So the epic's MOTIVATING defect (Bedrock-hosted Claude silently losing prompt caching) had no executable proof that caching is actually produced, only that the style string resolves. Note this escaped BOTH my own 18/18 held-out validation AND the Gerrit LLM-Review +1 — the completion-verifier close gate is what caught it, which is exactly the independent-check value the two-gate design is for. FIXED: added test_cache_settings_for_bedrock_style_sets_both_bedrock_breakpoints (boto3-gated, since BedrockModelSettings lives in the botocore-importing module), asserting the settings object is non-None, both bedrock cache keys True, and that the anthropic-shaped keys are NOT present (they would error on the Bedrock wire). Verified it BITES: mutating the bedrock branch to return None fails with 'Bedrock caching must be ON — this is the defect being fixed'. Also tidied docstrings my earlier automated rewrapper had mangled. 19/19 green, lint + format + mypy(383) clean. Amended 09cfdddc8 -> 460e431ee with Change-Id I71f2d56ea54257ea641d03617bf57e4c8a3393cf PRESERVED and re-pushed as a new patchset on change 1014; amending correctly reset both votes, so they must be re-earned before close.
